To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) pre-trained LNet is a powerful tool for face localization in the wild and (2) the semantic concepts discovered by ANet are useful for attribute prediction.

(1) pre-training strategies are crucial to fine-tuning, (2) face localization and attribute prediction can be jointly trained with only image-level tags without face bounding boxes, and (3) the hidden neurons in the deep learning network can automatically discover the semantic concepts.

(1) the performance of face localization can be improved by massive general object pre-training, and (2) the performance of attribute prediction can be improved by fine-tuning with massive face identities pre-training, and the hidden concepts of ANet can be well explained by linear combinations of the semantic concepts discovered after fine-tuning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental problem of face attribute recognition in the wild, which has been long ignored by previous works.
both the performance improvement and the learning mechanism of face representation.
two major aspects: 1) how to improve attribute prediction performance, and 2) how to understand face representations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proposed deep learning framework can automatically extract semantic concepts from massive face images, and such concepts can be used to learn a compact and discriminative representation for attribute prediction in an end-to-end manner.

our proposed deep learning framework for face attributes can not only achieve the state-of-the art, but also reveal the underlying mechanism of learning face representation, and thus it is very useful for future research.
our framework can effectively exploit the rich semantic information from massive face identities for face attribute learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
face attributes can be well learned by deep learning, but pre-training strategies are crucial to improve the performances.
the proposed framework is not only a state-of-the-art attribute prediction method, but also a powerful tool for understanding face representation.

we propose a new face representation learning framework, which can be pre-trained with massive general object categories, massive face identities and attribute tags, and can be fine-tuned with attribute tags only.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning is not a black box.
the pre-trained CNN can be fine-tuned to predict face attributes in the real world.
the performance of attribute recognition in the wild can be improved by pre-training the deep CNNs with massive general object categories and face identities.
